clue.text: Hunter signed agreement accepting I am right

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so the agreement wraps round what follows

blocks.note: a nod of the head signals agreement without words
contracted to I'm
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A hunter gives a signing nod to a deal that lets him be in the right.
explanation.walkthrough: NOD takes in I'M and R: N(IM R)OD. 'Signed' here means made a sign, not wrote a signature.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimrod is the mighty hunter of Genesis, and his name became a byword for any keen huntsman.

clue.text: I am familiar with a South African antelope

blocks.note: contracted to I'm
a familiar is a close friend
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone claiming to know a particular African antelope well.
explanation.definitionFit: The impala is a graceful reddish-brown antelope of southern and eastern African savannah.

clue.text: What boxing promoters do in small car

definitions.note: a verb phrase, the cryptic split of the answer

blocks.note: first meaning, read as three words: they stage a fight
second meaning: a light vehicle for short trips

explanation.surface: Fight promoters going about their business in a little car.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as RUN A BOUT, it is what a promoter does with a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A runabout is a compact car or boat used for short local journeys.

clue.text: Denunciation of help with raising family

indicators.note: in a down clue raising means lifting upward, so the word for help reads bottom to top

blocks.note: to aid is to help
a tribe is an extended family or clan

explanation.surface: A condemnation of state support for bringing up children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raising family' looks like child-rearing, but raising works only on the word for help.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter verbal attack, a forceful public condemnation of someone or something.

clue.text: Tract father with some speed leased out

blocks.note: an informal word for father
miles per hour, a unit of speed
to let a property is to rent it out

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a piece of land that a father, in a hurry, has rented out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tract' looks like an area of land, but here it is a short printed treatise.
explanation.definitionFit: A tract is a short leaflet or booklet arguing a religious or political point, which is exactly what a pamphlet is.

clue.text: American sportsman that can hold a lot of drink

definitions.text: that can hold a lot of drink

blocks.note: first meaning: the baseball player who throws to the batter

blocks.clueFragment: that can hold a lot of drink
blocks.note: second meaning: a large jug

explanation.surface: An American athlete with a hearty capacity for alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a hard-drinking player; the second meaning is a container, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: In baseball the player who throws is called this, and the same word names a big jug for liquids.

clue.text: Quite a large helping -- Paul left fragments

indicators.note: read as a verb, to fragment is to break up, so those letters are scattered and reassembled

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Paul served himself a big portion but left scraps behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fragments' looks like the leftovers on the plate; it is a verb telling you to break up the two names before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A plateful is the amount a dinner plate holds, a generous serving of food.

clue.text: Un jeu - kind of clue the French can comprehend

indicators.note: to comprehend is literally to take in, so the French word holds the clue type inside

blocks.note: the masculine French word for the
crossword clues are either across or down

explanation.surface: A French remark about a crossword clue the French can understand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Un jeu' is French for a game; the answer is a game whose name comes from French.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacrosse is a team sport played with netted sticks, and 'un jeu' is French for a game.

clue.text: Conspirator set it out as ordered

indicators.note: the letters are put in a new order, arranged as instructed

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A plotter laying out his scheme exactly as he was told.
explanation.walkthrough: Note that 'as' is part of the fodder as well as the indicator's start; only 'ordered' signals the shuffle in the surface sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Titus Oates fabricated the Popish Plot of 1678, a supposed Catholic scheme to murder Charles II.

clue.text: Start with actors like mine, taking it from the top

definitions.text: like mine, taking it from the top

blocks.note: to open is to start
the cast is the actors in a production

explanation.surface: Reads like a theatre director kicking off rehearsals, running the scene from the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking it from the top' sounds like rehearsal talk, but it describes digging out ore from the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An opencast mine works the ground from the surface downwards instead of through shafts and tunnels.

clue.text: Some drama Scott put in "The Talisman"

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the next words are used, a run sitting inside them
the answer has been placed inside the neighbouring words, tucked within them

blocks.note: the run spans the end of one word and most of the next

explanation.surface: Seems to ask about a play adapted from Walter Scott's novel The Talisman.
explanation.walkthrough: The Talisman really is a Scott novel, which makes the title look like literature rather than the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A talisman is a lucky charm, and a mascot is a person, animal or object kept to bring good luck.

clue.text: That lady and I must get points – I'm starting now

blocks.note: a pronoun for a woman
Latin for I, the self
east and south, two points of the compass

explanation.surface: A couple about to begin a game where both players need to score points.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is what someone says just before attempting something risky, announcing that they are beginning.

clue.text: Car reversed, arrived outside plant

indicators.note: turned round, so the word for a car is read from right to left
the word for arrived goes around the other piece

blocks.note: short for limousine
past tense of come

explanation.surface: A motorist backs up and pulls in beside a factory or a garden plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Camomile is a daisy-like herb whose flowers are dried to make a soothing tea.

clue.text: Stargazer's business very bad, with Io not visible

indicators.note: what cannot be seen is missing, so those two letters vanish from the word for very bad

blocks.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
pernicious means harmful, very bad
taken as written; Io is a moon of Jupiter

explanation.surface: An astronomer's line of work is in a bad way because Jupiter's moon Io cannot be seen.
explanation.walkthrough: Io, the moon, fits the stargazing picture, but it is just two letters removed from PERNICIOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Copernicus was the Polish astronomer who argued that the Earth orbits the Sun.

clue.text: Nepotism affected one dismissed - more than one worker given sack

definitions.text: more than one worker given sack

indicators.note: one, the Roman numeral, is sent away from the word before
something affected is altered, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Office favouritism leads to one person being fired, and soon several are sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove I from NEPOTISM, then rearrange. 'Given sack' sounds like fired, but these workers are handed a mail sack.
explanation.definitionFit: Mail carriers are plural workers who each carry a bag of letters on their rounds.

clue.text: Odd as fish may be, but not birds or animals

definitions.text: as fish may be, but not birds or animals

blocks.note: first meaning: strange, unusual

blocks.clueFragment: as fish may be, but not birds or animals
blocks.note: second meaning: grammatical number; one fish is still fish, but those plural words cannot be one

explanation.surface: Remarking how strange fish are compared with other creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish' can be singular or plural, while 'birds' and 'animals' are plural only, so they can never be the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means peculiar or remarkable, and in grammar it is the form naming just one thing.

clue.text: Suspect drops of water cause corrosion

blocks.note: mist is fine droplets of water in the air
rust is the corrosion of iron

explanation.surface: Damp is suspected of causing rust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspect' reads as a verb about blame; it is the definition, meaning to doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspect someone is to doubt or distrust them, the verb sense of the answer.

clue.text: Stripper against going into water in Channel

indicators.note: one piece enters the other, so it sits inside it

blocks.note: short for versus
the Solent is the strait between the Isle of Wight and mainland England, off the English Channel

explanation.surface: A striptease artist protesting against a cross-Channel swim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stripper' suggests a performer, but it is paint stripper, a chemical that dissolves.
explanation.definitionFit: A solvent dissolves other substances, and paint strippers are solvents used to lift old coatings.

clue.text: Wild olive -- Spanish approval given to flower

blocks.note: the Spanish cry of approval, olé
the aster is a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: A Spanish crowd cheers as a flower is presented, with olives nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: The oleaster is a shrub of the Mediterranean, also called Russian olive, bearing small olive-like fruits.

clue.text: Lord! Rebate initially reduced by 99%

indicators.note: the first letter, a Roman numeral, is replaced by one worth a hundredth as much

blocks.note: a rebate is a discount

explanation.surface: An exclamation at a rebate being slashed almost to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: D is 500 in Roman numerals; cut by 99% it becomes 5, which is V.
explanation.definitionFit: A viscount is a British nobleman ranked between earl and baron, addressed as Lord.

clue.text: Sculpture in box, perhaps

blocks.note: surface reading: a statue packed in a crate
setter's reading: shapes cut from box, the evergreen hedging shrub

explanation.walkthrough: Box is the shrub, not a container; 'perhaps' flags it as one example among yew, privet and others.
explanation.definitionFit: Topiary is the art of clipping living shrubs into ornamental shapes such as birds or spirals.

clue.text: Abroad, has a supervisor's job, we hear

indicators.note: what is heard is a sound, so the spelling may differ from the phrase's word

blocks.note: a supervisor watches over work, or oversees it

explanation.surface: Someone working abroad in a management role, as people say.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a foreign country across the sea is the plain meaning of this adverb.

clue.text: Girl's son suffering young Albert's fate?

indicators.note: young Albert was swallowed whole, so the son ends up inside the beast

blocks.note: the abbreviation for son
in Stanley Holloway's comic monologue, young Albert is eaten by a lion at the zoo

explanation.surface: A mother's boy suffering the same fate as the lad in a famous monologue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Albert and the Lion' is a 1930s British comic monologue in which a boy is swallowed by a lion; S goes inside A LION.
explanation.definitionFit: Alison is a girl's first name, so it fits any girl in a clue.

clue.text: It's the last drink that goes to one's head

blocks.note: first meaning: a drink taken just before bed
second meaning: a soft cap worn in bed, which literally sits on the head

explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes to one's head' sounds like intoxication, but it also means literally sitting on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a final alcoholic drink before bed and a soft hat once worn while sleeping.

clue.text: Being Red, for example, is non-U in America

blocks.note: surface reading: being a communist is not upper class in the United States
setter's reading: the American spelling of this word drops its U

explanation.surface: Being a Red, a communist, is socially unacceptable in the USA.
explanation.walkthrough: Non-U is British slang for not upper class, but here it means lacking the letter U, as American spelling does.
explanation.definitionFit: Red is one example of a hue, so a colour can be illustrated by naming red.

clue.text: Almost everyone has confidence about one who is unselfish?

indicators.note: almost all of the word is kept, the last letter being dropped
the word for confidence goes around the single letter

blocks.note: everyone is all
to have confidence in someone is to trust them
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Wondering whether someone who trusts nearly everybody is truly selfless.
explanation.definitionFit: An altruist puts the welfare of others before personal gain, the very picture of selflessness.

clue.text: Artifice whereby wandering sheep is penned

indicators.note: something penned is shut in a pen, so it sits inside the other word

blocks.note: to stray is to wander
a teg is a sheep in its second year

explanation.surface: A shepherd's clever trick for getting a stray sheep into the fold.
explanation.walkthrough: TEG, a young sheep, is a crossword staple worth learning.
explanation.definitionFit: Artifice is a cunning plan or device, and a strategy is a scheme for gaining an advantage.

clue.text: Reprimand for sailor

blocks.note: first meaning: a severe scolding
second meaning: an ordinary seaman in the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A sailor gets a telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: A rating is both a sharp telling-off and a naval seaman who is not an officer.
